_comment: The k-server A/A run on the laptop's Windows (Alex, 2026-10-28: "More A/A servers"): v2 7 times in each of the three programs (21 contestants, 21 servers per cell, 294 windows), the campaign's cells, rounds and window values. It measures how much separate processes of one build differ: in every other run each contestant is one server process, so its spread is the spread within that process. 21 servers per cell is the Windows campaign's count (Arch's has 22), so idle neighbours on the server CPU and the gaps between a contestant's windows are close to the campaign's. Its statistics are fixed in t3/rr_results.py (the k-server A/A record), committed with this plan before it runs; they describe and do not enter the floor. Round-robin (p2run's schedule): mixed-disjoint, m = 1,000 and 100,000, pair (127, 227); per cell every contestant's server starts once, in plan order, and gets a 1 s warm-up, then 7 rounds give each contestant one 1.5 s window (after p2gen's 0.1 s lead-in) in an order drawn from order_seed; others above 10% of one CPU make a window invalid and its round reruns once in the cell (decision 18). It times the Release builds of the bring-up at 3ff814e (gated green, the builds every round-3 record timed); t3/jobs/aa.py refuses unless each binary's sha256 is the bring-up's and no compiled source changed since _build_commit.
